title: Soft-fencing for GPU tenants: hybrid token-bucket caps with backpressure and graceful eviction
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Implement a soft-fencing mechanism for GPU tenants that enforces throughput caps with a hybrid token-bucket + backpressure design. Goal: provide predictable per-tenant throughput guarantees in Dedicated while avoiding hard preemption where possible, and enable controlled degradation (graceful eviction) under contention. This ticket covers scheduler-side enforcement, tenant telemetry, console controls for setting caps/policies, and an autoscale interaction contract.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant rate caps configurable via Console and returned in API (tokens/sec and burst size)
Scheduler implements token-bucket enforcement with a configurable soft_threshold and hard_threshold
When soft_threshold exceeded, scheduler signals backpressure to requestor (505 backpressure header) and prefers batching tolerant requests for remaining capacity
When hard_threshold exceeded for sustained period, eviction scoring triggers graceful eviction of low-priority lanes with detailed audit logs
New telemetry available: per-tenant capacity_usage_pct, backpressure_count, eviction_count, avg_request_latency_p95
E2E tests covering normal, burst, and sustained overload scenarios; performance benchmark doc comparing current and new scheduler with 1%, 10%, 50% overcommit workloads
technical_decisions: Enforce quotas at the scheduler ingress rather than at the GPU driver level to keep implementation portable across Dedicated and Private deployments
Use a hybrid model: token-bucket for steady-state enforcement + strain score for eviction priority, so short bursts are allowed but sustained abuse triggers eviction

Backpressure will be surfaced via a new HTTP header 'X-RW-Backpressure' and a 202/429 semantic depending on client contract; streaming/gRPC paths will receive a control frame indicating delay allowance
Autoscaler contract: autoscaler may raise tenant soft_threshold temporarily if predictive surge detected but must not change hard_threshold without operator approval
Audit logs and KMS-integrated keying will be used for any actions that change tenant thresholds (to satisfy compliance requirements)
implementation_notes: Scheduler component: add token-bucket store keyed by tenant-id with atomic compare-and-swap updates
KV cache and batching must be accounted for — we add 'prefetch' tokens deduction to avoid double-counting token use for cached KV hits
Eviction scoring factors: tenant SLA tier, recent error_budget, per-tenant QoS profile, and historical noisy-neighbor fingerprint
Introduce a lightweight noise-detection classifier that flags tenants with >X% small-high-frequency requests; these tenants are deprioritized in eviction score
Console: UI control to set soft/hard thresholds and a 'grace window' in minutes for eviction to allow customer graceful degrade handling
risk_and_tradeoffs: Soft-fencing reduces customer-visible hard failures but can mask misbehaving tenants causing higher tail latency for others if thresholds set too leniently
Placing enforcement in scheduler keeps runtime portable but adds a small per-request CPU overhead — measured ~0.15ms/request in benchmarking
Aggressive use of predictive autoscaler adjustments may lead to oscillations; contract limits introduced to avoid flip-flopping
Noise-detection heuristics may generate false positives; conservative defaults and opt-out label for trusted partners included
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy soft-fencing in a single Dedicated cluster with internal customers — monitor backpressure_count and p95 latency (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): expose console controls to a select group of customers with opt-in; collect feedback and tweak eviction scoring (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): enable soft-fencing by default with reasonable conservative defaults and telemetry dashboards; provide migration guide to customers (2 weeks)
Rollback plan: revert to token-bucket disabled flag; immediate lift of soft enforcement if severe consumer impact observed
metrics_and_dashboards: dashboard: 'Tenant Isolation Overview' in Console showing top offenders, alert thresholds, and per-tenant SLO impact
alerts: fire when any tenant backpressure_count spikes 5x baseline or when cluster-wide 95th latency increases by >20%
